title: AC1 One bulk request is created for a multi-device NCCM operation

steps.action: Login as admin (admin/admin); run a Runbook Execution against 100 NCCM devices
steps.expected: Operation is submitted for approval

steps.action: Login as admin (admin/admin); navigate NCCM > Approval
steps.expected: Exactly ONE approval request represents all 100 devices — not 100 individual requests

title: AC2 Bulk badge is shown in the approval listing

steps.action: Login as admin (admin/admin); navigate NCCM > Approval with a bulk request present
steps.expected: Listing loads

steps.action: Inspect the bulk request row
steps.expected: A "Bulk" badge distinguishes it from single-device requests

title: AC3 Parent request shows aggregated Pending / Approved / Rejected counters

steps.action: Create a bulk request over 100 devices, approve 50 and reject 30
steps.expected: Actions complete

steps.action: Read the parent request row
steps.expected: Counters read Pending 20 | Approved 50 | Rejected 30 and total 100

title: AC3 Counters update live as device decisions are made

steps.action: Open a bulk request with all devices pending and note the counters
steps.expected: Pending equals the device count

steps.action: Approve 5 devices and re-read the parent row
steps.expected: Pending drops by 5 and Approved rises by 5 without a manual refresh, and the three counters always sum to the device total

title: AC4 Clicking a bulk request opens a drawer listing all its devices

steps.action: Login as admin (admin/admin); navigate NCCM > Approval and click a bulk request
steps.expected: A drawer opens

steps.action: Inspect the drawer
steps.expected: Every device in the request is listed with its own status

title: AC5 Approver can select all pending devices at once

steps.action: Open a bulk request drawer containing pending, approved and rejected devices
steps.expected: Drawer lists all devices

steps.action: Use Select All Pending
steps.expected: Only the pending devices become selected; approved and rejected devices are not selected

title: AC5 Approver can select an individual pending device

steps.action: Open a bulk request drawer
steps.expected: Drawer lists devices

steps.action: Tick one pending device
steps.expected: That device alone is selected and the approve/reject actions become available

title: AC5 Approver can multi-select several pending devices

steps.action: Open a bulk request drawer with at least 5 pending devices
steps.expected: Drawer lists devices

steps.action: Tick three pending devices
steps.expected: All three are selected and a single approve action applies to exactly those three

title: AC6 Already approved devices are visible but not selectable

steps.action: Open a bulk request drawer containing previously approved devices
steps.expected: Drawer lists them

steps.action: Attempt to select an approved device
steps.expected: It is displayed with Approved status but its selection control is disabled

title: AC7 Already rejected devices are visible but not selectable

steps.action: Open a bulk request drawer containing previously rejected devices
steps.expected: Drawer lists them

steps.action: Attempt to select a rejected device
steps.expected: It is displayed with Rejected status but its selection control is disabled

title: AC8 Only pending devices remain selectable

steps.action: Open a drawer with a mix of pending, approved and rejected devices
steps.expected: Drawer lists all

steps.action: Use Select All Pending and count the selection
steps.expected: The selected count equals the Pending counter exactly

title: AC9/AC10 Clicking a device name shows its requested change comparison

steps.action: Open a bulk request drawer and click a device name
steps.expected: A comparison view opens

steps.action: Inspect the comparison
steps.expected: It shows the requested change for that specific device — running vs proposed configuration

title: AC11 Comparison matches the existing single-device approval experience

steps.action: Open the comparison for a device inside a bulk request, then open a single-device approval comparison
steps.expected: Both views open

steps.action: Compare the two
steps.expected: Same layout, same diff rendering and same controls — the bulk drawer reuses the existing experience rather than a divergent one

title: AC12/AC13 Approval requires a mandatory comment

steps.action: Select pending devices in a bulk drawer and trigger Approve, leaving the comment blank
steps.expected: Approve dialog opens

steps.action: Submit without a comment
steps.expected: Validation blocks submission — the approval comment is mandatory and nothing is approved

title: AC14 Approved device status becomes Approved and its task executes automatically

steps.action: Approve two selected pending devices with a comment
steps.expected: Approval is accepted

steps.action: Watch those two devices in the drawer
steps.expected: Each becomes Approved and its requested task starts executing automatically without a further trigger

title: AC14 Execution status is recorded per device

steps.action: Approve devices so their tasks execute, letting at least one succeed and one fail
steps.expected: Executions complete

steps.action: Inspect each device row
steps.expected: Each carries its own execution status; a failure on one device does not hide or alter another device's status

title: AC15 Approved devices are no longer selectable

steps.action: Approve a selection of devices
steps.expected: They become Approved

steps.action: Attempt to select them again
steps.expected: Their selection controls are disabled — an approved device cannot be re-approved or then rejected

title: AC16/AC17 Rejection applies to selected pending devices with a comment

steps.action: Select pending devices, trigger Reject and submit with a comment
steps.expected: Rejection is accepted

steps.action: Inspect those devices
steps.expected: Each becomes Rejected, no task executes for them, and they are no longer selectable

title: Partial approval leaves the remaining devices pending

steps.action: On a 100-device bulk request approve 40 and take no action on the other 60
steps.expected: Approval completes

steps.action: Read the parent counters
steps.expected: Pending 60 | Approved 40 | Rejected 0 — the risk-based partial-approval business case

title: Devices in one bulk request can have different outcomes

steps.action: On one bulk request approve some devices, reject others and leave the rest pending
steps.expected: All actions complete

steps.action: Inspect the drawer
steps.expected: Three distinct device states coexist under a single approval workflow

title: Bulk approval works for Firmware Upgrade

steps.action: Run Firmware Upgrade against 10 NCCM devices as a single operation
steps.expected: One bulk approval request is created

steps.action: Approve 5 devices and inspect the result
steps.expected: Only the 5 approved devices have their Firmware Upgrade executed; the other 5 stay pending with no execution

title: Bulk approval works for Configuration Sync

steps.action: Run Configuration Sync against 10 NCCM devices as a single operation
steps.expected: One bulk approval request is created

steps.action: Approve 5 devices and inspect the result
steps.expected: Only the 5 approved devices have their Configuration Sync executed; the other 5 stay pending with no execution

title: Bulk approval works for Backup Restore

steps.action: Run Backup Restore against 10 NCCM devices as a single operation
steps.expected: One bulk approval request is created

steps.action: Approve 5 devices and inspect the result
steps.expected: Only the 5 approved devices have their Backup Restore executed; the other 5 stay pending with no execution

title: Bulk approval works for Runbook Execution

steps.action: Run Runbook Execution against 10 NCCM devices as a single operation
steps.expected: One bulk approval request is created

steps.action: Approve 5 devices and inspect the result
steps.expected: Only the 5 approved devices have their Runbook Execution executed; the other 5 stay pending with no execution

title: Reminder can be sent only for devices still pending

steps.action: On a bulk request with pending, approved and rejected devices, send a reminder
steps.expected: Reminder is sent

steps.action: Inspect who was reminded
steps.expected: Only the pending devices are included; approved and rejected devices are unaffected

title: Cancellation is available per device and leaves decided devices alone

steps.action: Cancel a subset of pending devices in a bulk request
steps.expected: Cancellation completes

steps.action: Inspect the request
steps.expected: Only the cancelled devices change state; approved, rejected and other pending devices are untouched, and cancelled devices execute nothing

title: Per-device audit trail records approver, comment and outcome

steps.action: Approve some devices and reject others with distinct comments
steps.expected: Actions complete

steps.action: Open the audit trail for the request
steps.expected: Every device has its own record with approver identity, decision, comment, timestamp and execution status

title: GAP Notification behaviour for bulk actions is not agreed

steps.action: Approve devices in a bulk request and collect the resulting notifications
steps.expected: Notifications are delivered

steps.action: Count the emails
steps.expected: The ticket comments CONFLICT — one states bulk notifications trigger individually per device, another states bulk approval sends a single email, and the latest comment asks for templates that have not been supplied. This case cannot pass until the team fixes the expected behaviour

title: Single-device approval flow is unchanged

steps.action: Run an NCCM operation against exactly one device
steps.expected: An approval request is created

steps.action: Inspect the listing and approve it
steps.expected: It behaves as before with no Bulk badge and no drawer regression — introducing bulk must not alter the single-device path

title: A single-device operation does not create a bulk request

steps.action: Run an operation against one device, then against two devices
steps.expected: Both are submitted

steps.action: Compare the listings
steps.expected: The one-device operation produces a normal request; the two-device operation produces a bulk request. Confirm with the team whether the bulk threshold is 2 or configurable — the ticket says "multiple" without defining it

title: Concurrent approvals by two approvers do not double-execute a device

steps.action: Open the same bulk request as two approvers and approve the same device simultaneously
steps.expected: Both submit

steps.action: Inspect the device
steps.expected: It is approved once and its task executes once; the second submission is rejected or ignored as already-decided

title: Bulk request with a large device count stays usable

steps.action: Create a bulk request over 500 devices and open the drawer
steps.expected: Drawer opens

steps.action: Scroll, select all pending and approve
steps.expected: The drawer paginates or virtualises rather than hanging; counters stay correct and the approve action completes within a reasonable time

title: RBAC: a user without approval rights cannot approve or reject

steps.action: Log in as a user whose role lacks NCCM approval rights and open the approval listing
steps.expected: Access reflects the role

steps.action: Attempt to approve or reject devices in a bulk request
steps.expected: The actions are unavailable or rejected; no device state changes

title: RBAC: a requester cannot approve their own bulk request

steps.action: As a requester, raise a bulk NCCM operation and open the resulting request
steps.expected: Request is visible

steps.action: Attempt to approve it
steps.expected: Self-approval is blocked, or is explicitly permitted by documented policy — confirm the intended separation of duties with the team

title: XSS payload in the approval comment is neutralised

steps.action: Approve a device with the comment <script>alert(1)</script>
steps.expected: Comment is submitted

steps.action: View the comment in the drawer and the audit trail
steps.expected: Rendered escaped as literal text; no script executes

title: Execution failure on an approved device is surfaced, not swallowed

steps.action: Approve a device whose task will fail (e.g. make it unreachable first)
steps.expected: Approval succeeds and execution is attempted

steps.action: Inspect the device row
steps.expected: Execution status shows the failure with a reason; the device stays Approved and the failure does not block other devices' executions
